finding.shortLabel: Boston silence: every surviving Boston-era record class holds no John Gurney
finding.statement: Anderson's Great Migration Directory assigns John Gurney a Boston settlement beside Braintree, but no Boston record of any class names him. An exhaustive sweep of every surviving Boston-era record class - First Church admissions and baptisms, the Book of Possessions and Boston town records, the Aspinwall notarial register, Lechford's note-book, Suffolk Deeds Libers I-III, and the Boston vital records 1630-1699 - returns no Gurney of John's generation, and a manuscript-level full-text search adds none. This converts the 'Boston' attribution from an inference-level qualification into a record-level negative: John's documented life belongs wholly to his four towns, and the attribution is best read as a conflation with the 1636 Newgate apprentice, a Boston household servant who would have generated neither a church admission nor a property record.

finding.statement: The printed Boston-era civil record classes hold no Gurney of John Gurney's generation: the Book of Possessions and Boston town records, the Aspinwall notarial register of 1644-1651, Thomas Lechford's note-book of 1638-1641, the earliest Suffolk Deeds (Libers I-III, 1640-1660), and the Boston vital records 1630-1699 are each silent. The single Gurney in the Boston vital records is the 26 October 1693 marriage of Samuel Gurney and Sarah Shapley - probably John's grandson, an identification tested (not asserted) in the family Mendon-descendants unit - married thirty years after John's death, so no Boston civil record touches the emigrant himself.

finding.statement: The Early Records of the Town of Providence (town-meeting and probate volumes swept) hold no Gurney of any spelling; the only near-name is a distinct Thomas Garnet family of Providence. The 1655-1675 town and deed volumes are clean, which bounds John Gurney's unlocated 'Quinapaug' interest - a Providence-jurisdiction frontier share carried into his 1663 inventory - as one the Providence record never registered. (The separate 1690s Providence John-and-Sarah Gurney household sits in volumes outside this sweep and is unaffected.)
